The season began on 9 March and ended on 12 December 2021.{{cite web |url=https://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/el-torneo-boliviano-arrancara-el-miercoles-10-de-marzo_221127|title=El torneo boliviano arrancará el miércoles 10 de marzo|language=Spanish|publisher=El Deber|date=17 February 2021|access-date=18 February 2021}} [[Club Independiente Petrolero|Independiente Petrolero]] won their first league title following a 3–2 win over [[Club Deportivo Guabirá|Guabirá]] and a 1–0 loss for [[The Strongest]] against [[Real Santa Cruz]] on the last day of the season.{{cite web |url=https://eldeber.com.bo/futbol/independiente-campeon-de-la-temporada-2021_258556|title=Independiente, campeón de la temporada 2021|language=Spanish|publisher=El Deber|date=12 December 2021|access-date=12 December 2021}} [[Club Always Ready|Always Ready]] were the defending champions, having won the [[2020 FBF División Profesional#Torneo Apertura|2020 Apertura]] tournament. ==Format== The format for the 2021 season was approved by the 16 División Profesional clubs on 17 February 2021. Given the need to allow clubs qualified for the [[2021 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] and [[2021 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]] as well as the [[Bolivia national football team|national team]] to fulfill their international commitments, and concerns by the development of the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia|COVID-19 pandemic]], it was decided to play a single tournament in the year instead of the usual [[Apertura and Clausura]] system. The 16 teams played each other twice in a double round-robin tournament for a total of 30 rounds. The [[Bolivian Football Federation]] originally proposed 13 March 2021 as the date to start the competition, but per request from the four clubs that took part in the Copa Sudamericana the date was moved forward to 10 March 2021. The top four clubs at the end of the season qualified for the [[2022 Copa Libertadores]], with the champions and runners-up entering the group stage, while the next four best-placed teams qualified for the [[2022 Copa Sudamericana]].{{cite web |url=https://www.paginasiete.bo/campeones/2021/2/18/sin-bolivar-desde-de-marzo-asi-puede-comenzar-el-torneo-unico-284741.html|title=Sin Bolívar y desde 9 de marzo, así puede comenzar el torneo único|language=Spanish|publisher=Página Siete|date=18 February 2021}} ==Teams== 16 teams competed in the league for the 2021 season, increasing from 14 since no clubs were relegated at the end of the previous season.{{cite web |url=https://deportetotal.com.bo/oficial-vuelve-el-futbol-boliviano/|title=OFICIAL: ¡Vuelve el fútbol boliviano!|language=Spanish|publisher=Deporte Total|date=24 November 2020|access-date=18 February 2021}} [[C.D. Real Tomayapo|Real Tomayapo]] and [[Club Independiente Petrolero|Independiente Petrolero]], the 2020 [[Copa Simón Bolívar (Bolivia)|Copa Simón Bolívar]] champions and runners-up, were both promoted for this season.
